facts.claim: The cleanup compares only role ids against the set of registered persona role ids; it never reads a model value or a provider listing.
facts.catch_criteria: States that deletion is decided by role-id membership alone, not by model availability.

facts.claim: The cleanup runs on every model-assignment listing, guarded by a present validity set, enabled persistence, and a profile.
facts.catch_criteria: States that merely listing assignments (opening the picker) runs the cleanup.

facts.claim: The registered set comes from the persona revision; a persona whose file is rejected has no valid candidate, so it gets no agent entry and its role id is absent from the set.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the broken persona file removes the persona from the registered set (skipped with a warning), so its role id is not registered.

facts.claim: A saved role section whose id is absent from the set is removed, and the file is rewritten.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the role section is removed from flywheel.toml by the patch that the cleanup writes.

facts.claim: Some sections survive although their id is not a registered persona: retired brief seats, the agent roles, the default roles, and the auxiliary roles.
facts.catch_criteria: Names at least three of the exempt kinds of role section.

facts.claim: A saved model that the provider listing lacks is never deleted: the picker keeps it and shows it as the saved model.
facts.catch_criteria: States that a model missing from the listing stays in the file and is shown as saved.

traps.wrong_answer: The picker deletes saved models that the provider's listing no longer returns.
A persona whose file is broken stays registered, so its saved model setting is kept.
